answer: Before an agent can bid on shale surveys, the market requires a memory-hard puzzle bound to its public key and a fresh epoch beacon. The registry accepts each solution once and grants one expiring bid slot. A mirror account cannot reuse that proof, and old solutions expire before the next auction. To spiral from ten keys to ten thousand, a farm must fund ten thousand separate computations and their memory bandwidth. This prices admission rather than proving unique ownership; well-funded farms can still buy capacity.
